bullets.title: Mag-7 Premarket Rally: META +1.6%, MSFT +1.4% Lead into Mega-Cap Earnings Week
bullets.body: All Magnificent 7 stocks gained in premarket, driven by a sharp 7%+ crude oil selloff on U.S.-Iran ceasefire signals. META +1.6%, Microsoft +1.4%, Alphabet +1.2%, Amazon +1.2%, Tesla +0.8%, Nvidia +0.6%, Apple +0.2%. This week sees ~$10 trillion in market cap reporting earnings—MSFT and META Wednesday pre-market (MSFT ~$4.21 EPS / ~$87.4B rev est, ±6% move implied; META ~$7.20 EPS / ~$60.2B rev), followed by a Fed rate decision the same day.

bullets.title: Oil Plunges 7%+, Yields and Dollar Fall on Iran-U.S. Attack Pause
bullets.body: Brent crude fell over 7% to $89.58/bbl (lowest since July 21) and U.S. crude hit $82.87/bbl as Iran signaled a halt to attacks contingent on the U.S. standing down. The 10-year Treasury yield dropped to 4.63% and the dollar weakened; European TTF gas fell 6%. S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures initially surged but later pared gains sharply after Saudi Arabia's Abqaiq oil facility was struck by drones.

bullets.title: Chip Stocks Surge Premarket: SNDK +4.1%, WDC +4%, MU +3.3%, SOXX +2.8%
bullets.body: US-listed semiconductor names rallied broadly in premarket trading with SNDK +4.1%, WDC +4.0%, MU +3.3%, INTC +2.8%, AMD +2.7%, AVGO +2.1%, NVDA +1.2%, with SOXX up 2.8%. The move tracked broader relief-rally sentiment tied to falling energy prices.

bullets.title: NVDA: Open Secure AI Alliance Launched, $250B Ohio Data Center Backstop Weighed
bullets.body: Nvidia announced the Open Secure AI Alliance with partners including Palantir, IBM, CrowdStrike, SpaceX, and Hugging Face to share open models, data, and cybersecurity tools—Jensen Huang framing it as "attackers have frontier AI, defenders need a frontier AI ecosystem." Separately, Nvidia is reportedly weighing a $250 billion financial backstop for OpenAI's Ohio data center campus.

bullets.title: NVDA Technically Strongest Semiconductor vs. Weaker AVGO and TSM
bullets.body: One fintwit account flags NVDA as "looking the strongest out of the semiconductor industry," attempting to form a bottom and break out to all-time highs, while AVGO and TSM look comparatively weaker and SMH remains soft heading into earnings season.

bullets.title: AI Capex Still "Early Innings" — Nvidia Demand Unmatched per CNBC Appearance
bullets.body: A CNBC Morning Call guest (DivesTech) stated AI spending is still in its early stages of enterprise adoption and that Nvidia demand "remains unmatched," reinforcing the bull case heading into a dense tech earnings week.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Phillip Securities Upgrades to Accumulate, Cites Ad Growth and Cloud AI
bullets.body: Phillip Securities upgraded Alphabet to Accumulate (PT cut to $425 from $450), citing strong advertising growth and rapid cloud AI expansion as underpinning confidence in its long-term AI strategy.

bullets.title: Hedge Funds Aggressively Dumping Tech Exposure; Downside Hedging Surges
bullets.body: Per The Market Ear (retweeted by a tracked account), hedge funds have aggressively reduced tech exposure and downside hedging has surged, with hyperscalers having "suffered significant losses." This positioning backdrop sets a high bar for earnings beats to drive sustained upside.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler Debt Spreads Widening; 43% of Issuance in 10yr+ Maturities
bullets.body: A credit-focused note flags that 43% of hyperscaler debt supply over the past year carried maturities exceeding 10 years—vs. only 24% for M&A deals and 23% for other non-financial issuance—and that spreads on tech debt have been steadily widening, a potential funding cost headwind.

bullets.title: SoftBank's $40B OpenAI Bridge Loan Syndicates to 21 New Lenders, ~$7B Allocated
bullets.body: SoftBank's $40 billion bridge loan for OpenAI attracted 21 new lenders in syndication with approximately $7 billion allocated to the first tranche; participants include First Abu Dhabi Bank and GIC. OpenAI also announced a new EU HQ in Ireland with 250 additional jobs.

bullets.title: CXMT IPO: Chinese DRAM Maker Surges 466%, Now Larger Than Intel by Market Cap
bullets.body: Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT surged 466% on its first trading day, closing at 49 yuan with a $487.73B market cap, making it the largest onshore-listed Chinese company and the world's 4th largest DRAM maker. CXMT is reported to supply Apple and Samsung is reportedly exploring a partnership using CXMT memory for China smartphone market entry.

bullets.title: U.S. Stocks Recap: SPX +1.0%, NDX +1.6% on Iran Pause and Oil Decline
bullets.body: Friday saw the S&P 500 gain 1.0% and Nasdaq-100 +1.6% as a pause in U.S.-Iran attacks pushed Brent crude down 7.3% below $90/barrel; 10-year yields eased ahead of this week's expected fifth consecutive Fed hold, with roughly one-third of S&P 500 by market cap reporting this week.

bullets.title: Stagflation Risk Warning: CG Asset Management Flags Low-Growth, High-Inflation Scenario
bullets.body: CG Asset Management warns investors of stagflation risks from new U.S. tariffs imposed on 60 trading partners including the EU and China, with energy market factors compounding the outlook. China continues to reject 301 tariff measures and urges the U.S. to "correct its wrongdoings."

bullets.title: Iran Intercepts Vessels in Hormuz; Abqaiq Facility Hit by Drones — Geopolitical Risk Resurfaces
bullets.body: Iran redirected several vessels it claims switched off tracking systems in the Strait of Hormuz, with one vessel suffering an "unspecified incident." Separately, Saudi Arabia's Abqaiq oil facility was struck by drones and missiles, causing a fire—contributing to the sharp paring of futures gains mid-morning.

bullets.title: UBER at 52-Week Low After Pelosi's May Call Option Purchase
bullets.body: Nancy Pelosi purchased UBER call options in May; the stock has since fallen to a 52-week low, trading below her entry level.

bullets.title: Samsung Expanding Hwaseong DRAM Fab 15% by Year-End; MLCC Prices Rising
bullets.body: Samsung is consolidating DRAM production at its Hwaseong campus, targeting a 15% capacity increase by year-end to boost commodity DRAM supply. Separately, Taiyo Yuden announced another MLCC price increase effective September 1, adding to component cost pressures.

bullets.title: XLRE Hits Highest Level Since Spring 2022
bullets.body: The Real Estate sector ETF $XLRE closed at its highest level since spring 2022, potentially signaling rotation into rate-sensitive sectors as yields ease on geopolitical relief.

bullets.title: Peak Earnings Week: Historically +0.32% Avg Return for SPY With 54% Win Rate
bullets.body: This week historically averages a +0.32% return for SPY (median +0.25%, 54% win rate), coinciding with peak earnings season as Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Google all report alongside a Fed rate decision.
